questions.statement: Which word in English names the piece of clothing you wear to keep warm on cold Bogota mornings?
questions.context: On a cold morning in Bogota, a girl puts on a warm jacket before going to school.

options.text: Jacket.
options.feedback: A jacket is a warm outer piece of clothing worn in cold weather.

options.text: Shorts.
options.feedback: Shorts are short pants worn in hot weather, not in cold weather.

options.text: Sandals.
options.feedback: Sandals are open shoes for hot days, not for cold mornings.

options.text: Cap.
options.feedback: A cap protects from the sun, but it does not keep the body warm.

questions.explanation: Identifying basic clothes vocabulary by its use in cold weather in English (jacket, shorts, sandals, cap).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does Laura wear a T-shirt and shorts?
questions.context: Read: "It is a sunny day in Cartagena. Laura wears a T-shirt and shorts because it is very hot."

options.text: Because it is a sunny and very hot day in Cartagena.
options.feedback: The text directly states that the sunny hot weather is the reason for her clothes.

options.text: Because it is a cold morning with rain.
options.feedback: Cold and rain are not mentioned; the day is described as sunny and hot.

options.text: Because she goes to swim in a cold river.
options.feedback: Swimming in a river is not mentioned in the passage.

options.text: Because she likes winter and snow.
options.feedback: Winter and snow are not part of the Cartagena context.

questions.explanation: Inferring the reason for wearing certain clothes from a short descriptive text in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly describes what the boy does using the Simple Present?
questions.context: It is the rainy season in Medellin. A boy looks at the dark clouds and takes his umbrella.

options.text: He takes his umbrella because it is the rainy season.
options.feedback: "Takes" agrees with the third person singular subject "he".

options.text: He take his umbrella because it is the rainy season.
options.feedback: "Take" without -s is incorrect with "he" in Simple Present.

options.text: He taking his umbrella because it is the rainy season.
options.feedback: "Taking" is a gerund and needs an auxiliary verb in this construction.

options.text: He takes his umbrellas because it is the rainy season.
options.feedback: "Umbrellas" in plural is incorrect; he takes one umbrella.

questions.explanation: Using the verb "take" with the third person singular to describe clothes and objects for rainy weather in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct imperative sentence that follows this advice.
questions.context: A teacher in Cali says: "Put on your boots before you walk in the rain."

options.text: Put on your boots before going out in the rain.
options.feedback: The imperative base form "put" gives a direct instruction to the listener.

options.text: You puts on your boots before going out in the rain.
options.feedback: The imperative does not use a subject or the -s form of the verb.

options.text: Putting on your boots before going out in the rain.
options.feedback: "Putting" is a gerund; imperatives use the base form of the verb.

options.text: To put on your boots before going out in the rain.
options.feedback: The infinitive form is not used as an imperative command.

questions.explanation: Giving simple weather-related instructions using the imperative form in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly expresses a reason using "because"?
questions.context: A student writes about his morning: "I wear a sweater because it is very cold in Bogota today."

options.text: He wears a sweater because it is very cold in Bogota today.
options.feedback: "Because" introduces a clear cause-effect relationship in the present simple.

options.text: He wears a sweater but it is very cold in Bogota today.
options.feedback: "But" expresses contrast, not the reason for wearing a sweater.

options.text: He wears a sweater so it is very cold in Bogota today.
options.feedback: The logic is reversed: the cold weather causes him to wear a sweater.

options.text: He wears a sweater because it is very hot in Cartagena today.
options.feedback: Hot weather contradicts wearing a sweater and the Bogota context.

questions.explanation: Using "because" to connect weather causes and clothing choices in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does Sofia pack for each city?
questions.context: Read: "Sofia packs a suitcase for Cartagena: T-shirts, shorts, and sandals. For Bogota she packs a jacket, a sweater, and boots."

options.text: Light clothes for hot Cartagena and warm clothes for cold Bogota.
options.feedback: The text lists T-shirts and shorts for Cartagena and jacket, sweater and boots for Bogota.

options.text: A jacket and boots for Cartagena and shorts for Bogota.
options.feedback: The suitcase lists are reversed; warm clothes are for Bogota, not Cartagena.

options.text: Only an umbrella for both cities.
options.feedback: An umbrella is not mentioned in her suitcase lists.

options.text: The same winter coat for both cities.
options.feedback: She packs different clothes because the weather in each city is different.

questions.explanation: Identifying appropriate clothes for different Colombian climates from a short descriptive paragraph in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which comparison correctly explains why their clothes are different?
questions.context: Compare two children: "Diego wears shorts and a T-shirt in sunny Santa Marta. Camilo wears a sweater, a jacket, and boots on a cold morning in Tunja."

options.text: Diego dresses for hot sunny weather, while Camilo dresses for cold weather.
options.feedback: Shorts and T-shirt suit heat, while sweater, jacket and boots suit cold.

options.text: Diego also wears a sweater and boots in the heat.
options.feedback: The text says Diego wears shorts and a T-shirt, not warm clothes.

options.text: Camilo wears shorts because it is very cold in Tunja.
options.feedback: The text says Camilo wears warm clothes because it is cold.

options.text: Neither Diego nor Camilo chooses clothes for the weather.
options.feedback: Both children choose clothes that match the weather in their city.

questions.explanation: Comparing clothing choices described in English to draw conclusions about weather differences.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the most important message of this paragraph?
questions.context: Read: 'In Colombia there are rainy and sunny seasons. On sunny days in Cartagena children wear T-shirts and shorts. On cold mornings in Bogota they wear sweaters and jackets, and in the rainy season everyone carries an umbrella and wears boots.'

options.text: People in Colombia choose their clothes according to the weather and the season.
options.feedback: The text links sunny days, cold mornings and rainy season with different clothes.

options.text: Children should always wear a sweater in Cartagena.
options.feedback: Cartagena is described as sunny, so T-shirts and shorts are worn there.

options.text: Umbrellas and boots are only for sunny days at the beach.
options.feedback: The text assigns umbrellas and boots to the rainy season, not sunny days.

options.text: Jackets and sweaters are useless in Colombia.
options.feedback: The paragraph says jackets and sweaters are worn on cold Bogota mornings.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main message of a short expository paragraph about clothes and weather in Colombia.
questions.subject: ingles
